text.arabic_uthmani: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يُلْحِدُونَ فِىٓ ءَايَٰتِنَا لَا يَخْفَوْنَ عَلَيْنَآ ۗ أَفَمَن يُلْقَىٰ فِى ٱلنَّارِ خَيْرٌ أَم مَّن يَأْتِىٓ ءَامِنًۭا يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ ۚ ٱعْمَلُوا۟ مَا شِئْتُمْ ۖ إِنَّهُۥ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ

words.gloss_range: emphatic opener that fixes the accused class before denying hiddenness

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: emphatic explanatory clause opener with singular divine pronoun

words.prose: {{ar:إِنَّ}} ({{tr:inna}}) opens with confirmation rather than neutral report. It holds the accused class in view until the denial of hiddenness lands, so the later comparison and command proceed from an already established exposure claim. Its echo with {{ar:إِنَّهُۥ}} ({{tr:innahū}}) near the end frames the ayah: first the sign-distorters are not hidden, then the reason is given through divine sight over deeds.

topics.headline: emphatic exposure frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah begins from confirmed exposure, not from an undecided accusation.
topics.reason: The opening emphatic particle governs the relative head and delays the predicate until the hiddenness denial, while the closing emphatic clause supplies the rationale.

words.gloss_range: plural relative head forming a class by the following ongoing practice
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلَّذِينَ}} ({{tr:alladhīna}}) does not name a tribe or status first; it waits for the relative clause to define the group by action. The warning therefore gathers whoever fits the practice of distorting the signs, and the exposure that follows answers that practice rather than an undefined population.

topics.headline: class defined by practice
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the warned group is defined by what they keep doing with the signs, not by a static label.
topics.reason: The relative pronoun is the subject of the opening emphatic clause and receives its identity from the following relative predicate.

words.gloss_range: ongoing crooked or lateral distortion within the sign-field, with Form IV pressure toward active corruptive handling
words.root_gloss_range: root range around inclining, turning aside, lateral deviation, and side-niche imagery; the local Form IV imperfect selects practiced distortion in relation to signs
words.prose: {{ar:يُلْحِدُونَ}} ({{tr:yulḥidūna}}) makes the accusation sharper than generic disbelief: the group is practicing a sideways distortion inside the sign-field. The Form IV surface lets the act feel active and corruptive, while the accepted Form I contrast keeps direct turning-aside audible without replacing the canonical wording. The ḥ-d friction gives that crookedness a rougher sound against the open sign-field, so the previous proof's straight seeing is answered by bent internal handling. The rare root also links this sign-distortion to the warning over deeds, with the divine-name parallel (7:180) showing the same crooked handling moved from names to signs.

topics.headline: ongoing lateral distortion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a precise accusation of practiced crooked handling, not a vague charge of disagreement.
topics.reason: The imperfect plural relative predicate defines the group by continuing action, and the root evidence supports lateral deviation as the local image.

topics.headline: Form IV with accepted Form I contrast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the canonical form emphasizes active corruptive handling while the reading contrast preserves the turning-aside pressure.
topics.reason: The accepted contrast clarifies nuance, but the aligned local surface remains the Form IV imperfect and governs the prose.

topics.headline: rare distortion root becomes accountable deed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that crooked sign-reading is not treated as private interpretation only; it is drawn into the deed-field under sight.
topics.reason: The ayah later repeats the deed root in command and predicate, and the parallel with divine-name distortion (7:180) confirms the specialized distribution.

topics.headline: rough sound and boundary reversal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the previous proof's straight seeing reversed into rough-sounding internal distortion.
topics.reason: The sound row reinforces the semantic contrast, and the boundary row ties this accusation to the sign-proof immediately before it.

words.gloss_range: preposition marking the signs as the domain and concern within which distortion operates
words.prose: {{ar:فِىٓ}} ({{tr:fī}}) prevents the accusation from floating as a general charge. It turns the verb into the sign-field, making the signs both the concern of the distortion and the pictured field within which the crooked handling occurs.

topics.headline: signs as distortion domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the offense is located within the evidence-field rather than outside it.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the signs and attaches them to the deviation verb as its domain.

words.gloss_range: divinely possessed plural signs, verses, proofs, or tokens serving as the domain of distortion
words.root_gloss_range: sign and indication range, with a disputed return/refuge pressure kept as background orientation rather than the selected local sense

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: divine perception-plane completing the hiddenness idiom

words.prose: {{ar:ءَايَٰتِنَا}} ({{tr:āyātinā}}) names the field being mishandled as multiple owned signs: verses, proofs, and tokens can all be caught by this plural. The possessive ending ties the evidence to the divine speaker and then echoes in {{ar:عَلَيْنَآ}} ({{tr:ʿalaynā}}), so the One whose signs are distorted is also the One from whom the distorters are not hidden. The disputed return/refuge pressure is useful only as orientation: these signs are what one should turn toward, while the local phrase still selects signs as evidentiary indicators. Same-surah contrasts deepen that field: signs become guidance and healing for believers (41:44), and signs will later be shown in horizons and selves (41:53).

topics.headline: owned plural sign-field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the distortion targets a broad divine evidence-field, not one isolated sign.
topics.reason: The word is a possessed feminine plural governed by the preceding preposition, and the lexical evidence supports verse, proof, and token range.

topics.headline: signs as orientation with contested root pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the signs are not inert data; they are indicators one should turn toward rather than bend aside.
topics.reason: The local noun remains signs or indicators, while the disputed return/refuge and orientation pressure survives as interpretive coloring.

topics.headline: same-surah sign network
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this sign-distortion is a rupture inside a larger surah argument about signs, guidance, and disclosure.
topics.reason: The same-surah rows explicitly connect this sign-field to positive reception (41:44) and later disclosure (41:53).

topics.headline: ownership and oversight echo
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the repeated divine suffix binding owned evidence to divine exposure.
topics.reason: The repeated first-person plural suffix links the signs and the perception-plane within the opening clause.

words.gloss_range: negation denying hiddenness while allowing the deviant act to stand as exposed
words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) negates the hiddenness predicate, not the act of distortion. The ayah grants that the practice occurs only to deny its escape from divine perception, and this opening denial prepares the later question of outcomes before the final sight attribute answers it.

topics.headline: hiddenness denied, distortion exposed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the text denies concealment, not the existence of the offense.
topics.reason: The negative particle scopes over the following hiddenness verb and the clause later closes with the perception attribute.

words.gloss_range: being hidden or becoming concealed, here negated as a continuing possibility for the people themselves
words.root_gloss_range: concealment, subtle hiddenness, obscurity, and evasion; local syntax denies such hiddenness before the divine perception-plane

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: stable divine perception and discernment over deeds

words.prose: {{ar:يَخْفَوْنَ}} ({{tr:yakhfawna}}) makes the offenders themselves the subject of failed concealment. The imperfect form denies hiddenness as an ongoing possibility, and the root range lets the denial reach subtle evasion as well as outward secrecy. The general hiddenness claim of 14:38 is narrowed here onto sign-distorters, and the final {{ar:بَصِيرٌ}} ({{tr:baṣīr}}) explains why concealment collapses.

topics.headline: people themselves not hidden
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that exposure falls on the offenders themselves, not only on their act.
topics.reason: The verb is intransitive with the people as subject and is negated in imperfect form.

topics.headline: concealment defeated by sight
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a perception arc from failed concealment to the closing attribute of sight.
topics.reason: The opening hiddenness verb is answered by the final seeing predicate, with 14:38 serving as a broader hiddenness parallel.

topics.headline: subtle evasion also fails
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that both external secrecy and inner interpretive evasion are denied.
topics.reason: The root range includes subtle obscurity, while the local negation keeps the claim within denied hiddenness rather than expanding to a new action.

words.gloss_range: idiomatic perception-plane before which concealment fails, with first-person plural oversight

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: divinely possessed plural signs and evidences

words.prose: {{ar:عَلَيْنَآ}} ({{tr:ʿalaynā}}) completes the hiddenness idiom by naming the divine perception-plane, not a physical location. Its first-person plural ending echoes {{ar:ءَايَٰتِنَا}} ({{tr:āyātinā}}): the signs belong to Us, and the distorters are not hidden from Us. Because the opening beat lands here, the next question begins only after divine vantage has been sealed.

topics.headline: divine perception-plane
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that hiddenness is measured before divine oversight, not by human visibility.
topics.reason: The prepositional phrase is idiomatic with the hiddenness verb and closes the first assertion.

topics.headline: owned signs and oversight echo
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the repeated divine suffix enclosing distortion between owned evidence and divine oversight.
topics.reason: The same first-person plural suffix appears on the signs and on the perception-plane.

words.gloss_range: interrogative plus inferential connector that turns exposure into a rhetorical outcome comparison
words.prose: {{ar:أَفَ}} ({{tr:a-fa}}) fuses question and consequence. The comparison is demanded by the exposure just stated, so it is not a request for information but a rebuke that forces the listener to value the two final states correctly.

topics.headline: inferential rhetorical pivot
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the question grows out of the exposure claim and functions as warning, not inquiry.
topics.reason: The split particle combines interrogative force with a following consequence link and begins the comparison clause.

words.gloss_range: first singular relative comparison head representing the fire-cast outcome type
words.prose: The first {{ar:مَن}} ({{tr:man}}) opens the negative comparison pole and waits for its identity to be supplied by passive casting into the Fire. Singular form becomes typological: anyone matching this outcome is placed first, so the listener feels the negative pole before the secure alternative appears.

topics.headline: first pole defined by destination
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the comparison first defines a person by imposed destination, preparing the mirrored alternative.
topics.reason: The relative pronoun heads the first pole and is completed by the passive clause before the evaluative predicate.

words.gloss_range: passive caused encounter or being cast, foregrounding the affected person and suppressing the caster
words.root_gloss_range: meeting, encountering, receiving, and casting; the local Form IV passive selects imposed encounter or being cast into consequence

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: active coming or arrival in the secure comparison pole

words.prose: {{ar:يُلْقَىٰ}} ({{tr:yulqā}}) makes the first figure acted upon. The Form IV passive suppresses the caster and turns the root's meeting field into an imposed encounter: the person is made to face the Fire. That passive posture stands across from {{ar:يَأْتِىٓ}} ({{tr:yaʾtī}}), where the secure figure comes actively, and it contrasts with the broader meeting-the-Lord scene of striving return (84:6). Even the qāf stop lets the passive verb land abruptly before the Fire destination.

topics.headline: passive imposed encounter
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices helpless affectedness: the first figure does not arrive with agency but is delivered into consequence.
topics.reason: The aligned verb is Form IV passive and the local syntax suppresses the agent while foregrounding the patient.

topics.headline: meeting root narrowed to casting
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that being cast is also forced encounter with one's outcome, while the local form keeps casting as the selected sense.
topics.reason: The broader meeting field is real, but the Form IV passive and Fire complement select imposed casting here.

topics.headline: passive versus active pole
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the comparison contrasts not only destinations but agency and posture.
topics.reason: The passive verb in the first pole is balanced by an active coming verb in the second pole.

topics.headline: hard stop before Fire
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the abrupt sound landing before the Fire destination.
topics.reason: The sound observation supports the same abruptness already carried by the passive casting image.

words.gloss_range: preposition marking the Fire as enclosing destination and resultant state
words.prose: {{ar:فِى}} ({{tr:fī}}) turns casting into enclosure. The person is not merely directed toward the Fire; the Fire becomes the containing result and state. Its repetition after the earlier sign-domain preposition links crookedness within signs to being placed within the Fire.

topics.headline: Fire as enclosing result
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the first outcome as an enclosing condition, not a remote destination.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the definite Fire after a passive casting verb.

topics.headline: from sign-domain to Fire-container
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a repeated preposition linking distorted domain to final container.
topics.reason: The same preposition appears first with signs and then with Fire, while local complements keep the two uses distinct.

words.gloss_range: the definite eschatological Fire as concrete enclosing punishment and negative outcome pole
words.root_gloss_range: fire and brightness range; local noun selects destructive Fire rather than guidance-light

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: circumstantial state of security carried at arrival

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلنَّارِ}} ({{tr:al-nār}}) completes the first pole with the known Fire, not a vague bad result. The root's brightness range is narrowed here to consuming exposure, a concrete and spatial punishment. It stands against {{ar:ءَامِنًۭا}} ({{tr:āminan}}), so danger and safety become paired outcome terms, with open ā resonance letting the ear hear the paired outcomes before meaning separates them. Prepared-Fire language (2:24) helps explain why the definite noun can carry recognized threat, and same-surah Fire recurrences keep this word inside the surah's judgment thread.

topics.headline: known eschatological Fire
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the first outcome as the recognized Fire, not a generic image of danger.
topics.reason: The noun is definite, genitive under the preposition, and supported by the known prepared-Fire parallel (2:24).

topics.headline: brightness narrowed to consuming Fire
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices brightness becoming punitive exposure rather than guidance.
topics.reason: The broader fire-light family survives as image pressure, while the local definite concrete noun selects Fire.

topics.headline: Fire against security
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the comparison pairing engulfing danger with secure arrival.
topics.reason: The first pole pairs passive casting with Fire, while the second pairs active coming with security.

topics.headline: judgment-thread and paired sound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices Fire as part of the surah's judgment thread and hears it paired with the later safety word.
topics.reason: The same-surah recurrence and sound pairing support the local contrast without changing the selected sense.

words.gloss_range: qualitative better/preferable predicate used rhetorically to expose false value judgment between whole outcome clauses
words.root_gloss_range: goodness, betterment, preference, and chosen value; local elative-predicate use tests the value of final outcomes
words.prose: {{ar:خَيْرٌ}} ({{tr:khayrun}}) is the hinge where the first full outcome is placed under a value question. Its indefinite comparative force asks qualitative preference rather than measurable advantage, and the answer is already collapsing before the second pole completes it. The Hereafter-better claim (87:17) becomes a staged scene here: being cast into Fire cannot be evaluated as better than secure arrival on the Day.

topics.headline: evaluative hinge between poles
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the comparison turning on a value predicate after the negative pole has been fully pictured.
topics.reason: The nominative predicate follows the first pole and is completed by the connected alternative.

topics.headline: qualitative value test
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the question exposes a whole value-system, not just a destination preference.
topics.reason: The indefinite elative compares two clauses and functions rhetorically to deny false equivalence.

topics.headline: Hereafter better claim dramatized
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a broader Quranic comparison formula concentrated into this two-pole judgment scene.
topics.reason: The secure outcome is the obvious positive answer, and the Hereafter-better formula (87:17) supplies a concrete comparison parallel.

words.gloss_range: connected alternative particle formally pivoting the question from the Fire pole to the secure pole
words.prose: {{ar:أَم}} ({{tr:am}}) answers the earlier question particle and makes one connected alternative, not a second question. After the value hinge, it transfers attention from passive fire-casting to secure coming, while the nasal join with the next pronoun tightens the audible hinge between the outcomes.

topics.headline: connected alternative to secure pole
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a formal turn from judged loss to secure arrival, not a loose disjunction.
topics.reason: The alternative particle pairs with the earlier interrogative and introduces the second comparison pole.

words.gloss_range: second mirrored relative comparison head, defined by active secure arrival

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: connected alternative particle introducing the second comparison pole

words.prose: {{ar:مَّن}} ({{tr:man}}) mirrors the first person-pronoun but takes an active predicate. The identical pronoun shape makes the contrast depend on what happens to each figure: one is cast, the other comes secure. The doubled sound after {{ar:أَم}} ({{tr:am}}) fuses the second pole tightly to the alternative.

topics.headline: mirrored secure pole
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same person-word receives the opposite outcome through its active predicate.
topics.reason: The second relative head mirrors the first and is completed by active coming with a security state.

words.gloss_range: active intransitive coming or arrival at the final event, with the subject's state supplied by the following security word
words.root_gloss_range: coming, arriving, reaching, happening, and bringing in other forms; local Form I selects active arrival rather than causative bringing

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: passive being cast or imposed encounter in the first comparison pole

words.prose: {{ar:يَأْتِىٓ}} ({{tr:yaʾtī}}) gives the second figure active arrival, and because the verb has no object the weight falls on the following state of security. Its Form I coming contrasts with the passive casting of {{ar:يُلْقَىٰ}} ({{tr:yulqā}}): both reach an outcome, but one is delivered into Fire while the other arrives secure at the final event. The certainty of coming language in 16:1 helps the arrival feel inevitable, not casual, and the paired glottal catches in the verb and security word mark the positive pole audibly.

topics.headline: active arrival carrying security
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the secure figure arrives actively and is defined by his carried state, not by an object brought.
topics.reason: The verb is active, intransitive, and followed by a circumstantial state.

topics.headline: arrival contrasts passive casting
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices agency reversal as part of the comparison's meaning.
topics.reason: The active coming verb is set across from the passive casting verb in the two balanced poles.

topics.headline: certain coming with audible arrest
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the positive pole as a marked and certain arrival.
topics.reason: The concrete parallel (16:1) supports certain coming language, while the sound row marks the positive phrase.

words.gloss_range: accusative circumstantial state of secure, fear-free, trustworthy safety carried at arrival
words.root_gloss_range: security, safety, trust, faith, and freedom from fear; local active participle selects secure state with faith-security pressure
words.prose: {{ar:ءَامِنًۭا}} ({{tr:āminan}}) is not a later reward tacked onto arrival; as a circumstantial state, it travels with the one who comes. The root range joins safety, trust, and faith-security, so the word answers the Fire pole by naming freedom from fear and harm while also carrying fidelity-to-truth pressure. The security of faith in 6:82 and the sign-reception contrast in 41:44 stand behind this positive outcome.

topics.headline: security carried into arrival
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that safety is the condition in which the person arrives, not something postponed until after arrival.
topics.reason: The word is an accusative state of the active arriver and has participial stability.

topics.headline: faith and safety overlap
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices security as moral and eschatological safety, not mere calm feeling.
topics.reason: The root range includes trust and safety, and 6:82 links security with faith unmixed with injustice.

topics.headline: security answers Fire
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the second pole as the semantic opposite of Fire: protected arrival against engulfing danger.
topics.reason: The security word stands in the second comparison pole against the definite Fire and is echoed by same-surah sign reception (41:44).

words.gloss_range: accusative event-time adverb locating secure arrival at the decisive final Day
words.root_gloss_range: day, time, and decisive occasion; local construct use makes it the event-time of Resurrection

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: circumstantial state of security carried at arrival

words.prose: {{ar:يَوْمَ}} ({{tr:yawma}}) locates the secure arrival at the most exposing time. The word is not merely a calendar marker; in construct with Resurrection it becomes the decisive occasion where hiddenness, choice, and outcome converge. Placing it after {{ar:ءَامِنًۭا}} ({{tr:āminan}}) lets security be heard first, then tested at the final-evaluation horizon also signaled by the Day of Recompense (1:4). It also joins the surah's time-thread, moving from created days and punishment days toward final disclosure.

topics.headline: secure arrival timed to final event
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the security belongs at the final exposing occasion, not present appearance.
topics.reason: The accusative time adverb governs the Resurrection noun in construct and times the secure arrival.

topics.headline: Day formula and delayed timing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the familiar final-Day frame arriving after the security word for rhetorical weight.
topics.reason: The dominant event-time pair is realized locally, and the Day of Recompense formula (1:4) supplies a concrete juridical horizon.

topics.headline: same-surah judgment time-thread
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices this Day-word joining the surah's movement from created days and punishment days to final disclosure.
topics.reason: The same-surah profile marks the word as part of a temporal judgment thread.

words.gloss_range: the definite Resurrection or final standing that specifies the Day as juridical event-time
words.root_gloss_range: rising, standing, establishing, straightening, and uprightness; local noun names the final Resurrection-standing
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ}} ({{tr:al-qiyāmah}}) specifies the Day as the recognized final standing. Its root range of rising, standing, establishing, and uprightness answers the opening crookedness: lateral distortion must face upright judgment. The standing-before-the-Lord scene (83:6) clarifies the payoff, making the previously named security arrive at the very site of standing before judgment. The comparison lands here before the ayah turns abruptly into direct command.

topics.headline: recognized final standing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the timing as the known Resurrection-standing, not an indefinite crisis.
topics.reason: The definite genitive noun specifies the preceding Day in an iḍāfah construction.

topics.headline: upright standing answers crookedness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a semantic reversal from sideways sign-distortion to final upright standing.
topics.reason: The root's standing/uprightness range is locally selected by the Resurrection noun and contrasts with the opening lateral-deviation root.

topics.headline: secure arrival at standing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices security being tested at the very site of standing before judgment.
topics.reason: The security word immediately precedes the Day of Resurrection phrase, and 83:6 supplies a concrete standing-before-the-Lord parallel.

words.gloss_range: plural imperative functioning as threatened permission, turning chosen action into accountable produced deed
words.root_gloss_range: doing, working, producing, practicing, and deeds as outputs; local command form initiates the accountable action frame

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: second-person plural imperfect doing under divine sight

words.prose: {{ar:ٱعْمَلُوا۟}} ({{tr:iʿmalū}}) abruptly turns the outcome comparison into direct address. Grammatically it is a command, but in this frame it functions as threat-permission: do what you will, while the final clause makes every chosen act visible. The root treats conduct as produced work, so freedom becomes traceable deed; the same root returns in {{ar:تَعْمَلُونَ}} ({{tr:taʿmalūna}}), and the surah's own deed-witness warning (41:22) keeps this command inside an accountability network.

topics.headline: imperative as threatened permission
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the command sounds like license but functions as warning under divine sight.
topics.reason: The imperative is followed by an open volition clause and then by a sight predicate, licensing the threat-permission reading.

topics.headline: action as inspectable output
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that chosen conduct is treated as produced output that can be inspected and answered.
topics.reason: The root range supports deeds as produced practice, and the testing-deeds parallel (67:2) gives the field accountability force.

topics.headline: direct address returns as seen deed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the shift from third-person outcome evaluation to second-person responsibility, then from command to what God sees.
topics.reason: The plural imperative addresses the audience directly and the same root recurs in the final predicate clause.

topics.headline: deed-accountability network
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the command as part of the surah's broader move from proof to judicial accountability.
topics.reason: The rows connect this imperative to same-surah deed testimony (41:22), testing-deeds language (67:2), and the boundary shift from proof to warning.

words.gloss_range: open relative or indefinite object of the imperative, widening the threatened action range

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: fronted prepositional-relative phrase marking the deed-domain of sight

words.prose: The first {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) supplies the command's open object: whatever the addressees will. Its breadth makes the apparent freedom maximally wide, but the later {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) returns inside {{ar:بِمَا}} ({{tr:bimā}}), turning the open range of choice into the object-domain of divine sight.

topics.headline: open object of threatened command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the command opens the whole range of chosen action under warning.
topics.reason: The particle functions as the object of the imperative and is completed by the following volition verb.

topics.headline: choice becomes evidence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same pronoun-shape carrying freedom into accountability.
topics.reason: The first occurrence opens what may be willed; the second occurrence marks what is done as the domain of sight.

words.gloss_range: second-person plural willing that completes the open object and assigns agency for the chosen action-range
words.root_gloss_range: willing, choosing, and thinghood/selected matter; local Form I perfect presents direct volition without compulsion
words.prose: {{ar:شِئْتُمْ}} ({{tr:shiʾtum}}) completes the open object by making the range of action depend on the addressees' own will. Its second-person plural form assigns agency directly, and the root's will-and-thinghood field makes what they select become the thing-like object of action and later sight. The warned freedom pattern of 18:29 clarifies the force: will is real, but it is not autonomy from consequence. The glottal catch also gives the will-clause a small arrest before the final divine-sight rationale arrives.

topics.headline: will completes action range
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the command's object is defined by the addressees' own chosen range.
topics.reason: The perfect second-person plural verb completes the preceding relative object of the command.

topics.headline: direct will becomes selected object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that inner willing and outer work are not split apart; selected will becomes actionable matter.
topics.reason: The local Form I verb presents direct willing, and the root field links willing with selected thinghood.

topics.headline: will under sight, not autonomy
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that human will is opened only to be placed under divine sight.
topics.reason: The phrase is followed by the sight rationale, and the warned freedom parallel (18:29) gives concrete support.

topics.headline: audible arrest before rationale
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the will-clause pause before the final divine-sight rationale arrives.
topics.reason: The word closes the short command phrase, and its sound profile marks the turn to the final clause.

words.gloss_range: emphatic explanatory closure with singular divine pronoun grounding the sight rationale
words.prose: {{ar:إِنَّهُۥ}} ({{tr:innahū}}) opens the explanation for why the apparent freedom is not open-ended liberty. It shifts from the earlier first-person plural markers to a focused singular pronoun, so the divine speaker whose signs and oversight opened the ayah now grounds the final seeing attribute. The same singular-pronoun seal also links resurrectional power in 41:39 to deed-surveillance in 41:40.

topics.headline: rationale after threat-command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the final clause as the reason commanded freedom remains under sight.
topics.reason: The emphatic particle with pronoun opens the closing nominal clause after the threat-command.

topics.headline: plural speech to singular attribute
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices divine ownership and oversight focusing into a singular attribute statement.
topics.reason: The pronoun resumes the divine referent after plural speech and matches the attribute-seal movement across the verse boundary.

words.gloss_range: fronted relational preposition binding the deed-domain to the seeing predicate

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: stable divine perception and discernment over deeds

words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) fastens the following deed phrase to {{ar:بَصِيرٌ}} ({{tr:baṣīr}}) as the domain of perception, not as an instrument of seeing. Because the phrase comes before the predicate, deeds stand in front of the final attribute. The earlier whatever-choice is thus converted into the evidence-domain of divine sight.

topics.headline: deeds as sight-domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that divine sight is attached directly to the deed-field.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the relative phrase and relates it to the final seeing predicate.

topics.headline: fronted deeds before seeing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the open choice range reappearing before the seeing attribute as evidence.
topics.reason: The prepositional phrase precedes the predicate and echoes the earlier open object of the command.

words.gloss_range: relative head after the preposition, covering the actual deeds done by the addressees

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: preposition governing the final deed-domain phrase

words.prose: The second {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) is governed by {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) and completed by the following deed verb. It gathers what the addressees actually do, not a vague character trait. By repeating the earlier {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}), it pivots the phrase from whatever they will to whatever they do, turning freedom into evidence.

topics.headline: actual deeds under sight
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final claim covers the full range of actual deed-instances.
topics.reason: The relative particle is governed by the preposition and completed by the following second-person action verb.

topics.headline: freedom becomes accountability
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the repeated pronoun-shape tracking choice into deed.
topics.reason: The first occurrence opens the willed action range, while this second occurrence gathers the done action under sight.

words.gloss_range: second-person plural imperfect doing, completing the fronted deed-domain as ongoing observable conduct
words.root_gloss_range: doing, working, producing, practicing, and deeds as inspectable outputs; local imperfect presents continuing action under sight
words.prose: {{ar:تَعْمَلُونَ}} ({{tr:taʿmalūna}}) completes the fronted phrase with actual doing. The imperfect keeps the deed-field open across continuing conduct, and the root makes those acts produced outputs available to sight rather than vanishing intentions. It also returns the earlier command root: what they were told to do becomes what they are seen doing. The formula appears after commanded good in 2:110, but here it is specialized as surveillance over threatened freedom and sign-distortion.

topics.headline: ongoing deeds supply content
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that divine sight covers continuing actual conduct, not only completed past acts.
topics.reason: The imperfect verb completes the relative phrase governed by the fronted preposition.

topics.headline: deeds as visible products
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices deeds as inspectable outputs placed under perception.
topics.reason: The root range supports produced action, and the word is immediately bound to the seeing predicate.

topics.headline: command becomes observable practice
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the earlier imperative returning as ongoing description before divine sight.
topics.reason: The same root appears first as imperative and then as imperfect predicate within the sight-domain.

topics.headline: sight formula specialized as threat
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a familiar deeds-under-sight formula turned toward warned freedom and same-surah testimony.
topics.reason: The formulaic parallel after commanded good (2:110) and same-surah testimony scenes (41:20, 41:22) show the clause's surveillance force here.

words.gloss_range: stable perceptive and discerning attribute focused on the deed-domain and closing the ayah's exposure frame
words.root_gloss_range: seeing, perceiving, discerning, and insight; local qualitative predicate presents enduring divine perception over deeds

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: opening denial that the sign-distorters are hidden

words.prose: {{ar:بَصِيرٌ}} ({{tr:baṣīr}}) is the final landing of the ayah: stable divine perception over what they do. The root includes seeing and discerning, so it answers both failed external concealment and crooked internal handling of signs. The formula can close exhortation as in 2:110, but here it closes threat-permission; it also returns to the opening {{ar:لَا يَخْفَوْنَ}} ({{tr:lā yakhfawna}}), explaining why concealment fails. Across the boundary from 41:39, divine capacity hands off to divine perception.

topics.headline: stable seeing predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices divine sight as an enduring attribute, not a one-time inspection.
topics.reason: The word is an indefinite qualitative predicate in the final emphatic clause, and the pattern supports enduring capacity.

topics.headline: discernment over deed-domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the attribute perceives and discerns the morally charged deed-domain.
topics.reason: The fronted deed phrase restricts the local predicate to perception over what they do, while the root range supports insight and discernment.

topics.headline: formula closes threat-permission
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a familiar deeds-under-sight formula functioning here as threat, not simple encouragement.
topics.reason: The formulaic closure is locally preceded by threat-permission, while 42:27 supplies a servant-governance sight parallel.

topics.headline: opening exposure closed by sight
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah framed by a perception ring: failed concealment at the start and sight at the end.
topics.reason: The final word closes the ayah and explicitly answers the opening denial of hiddenness.

topics.headline: capacity attribute hands to perception
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the boundary moving from divine power over resurrection to divine sight over sign-distortion and deeds.
topics.reason: The boundary rows link the final attribute to the previous ayah's attribute seal and to same-surah sight/testimony scenes (41:20, 41:22).

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The sequence yulhiduna fi ayatina, la yakhfawna alayna, and basir.
baseline_models.mechanism: Ilhad is modeled as a lateral turn away from a presented marker. The denial of concealment and the closing claim of penetrating sight make that turn an attempted movement into a blind spot that does not exist.

activation_trace.role: A move toward an edge or side supplies the deviation's directional geometry.
An outwardly legible marker supplies the visible object whose course is being bent.
Covering or remaining unseen names the evasion explicitly denied by the construction.
Penetrating awareness closes the mechanism by making deeds inwardly known as well as externally observable.

changed_reading.before: The ayah generally condemns people who distort signs and warns that God knows.
changed_reading.after: The ayah stages deviation as a directional attempt to move explicit signs toward a side channel, while declaring that no such movement creates an epistemic blind spot.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The passive yulqa fi al-nar is set against the active ya'ti aminan on the Day of Rising.
baseline_models.mechanism: The question contrasts two trajectories, not merely two static conditions: forced disposal into fire and self-arrival in settled security. The comparative and resurrection frame make present choice terminate in a mode of arrival.

activation_trace.role: Throwing or casting supplies a forced transfer in which the person is grammatically acted upon.
The burning destination gives the passive transfer its punitive terminus.
Selection between alternatives turns the rhetorical comparison into a present practical choice.
Coming and reaching supply the opposed trajectory of active arrival.
Settled freedom from expected harm defines the quality of that arrival.
The rising of creation fixes both trajectories at the final public event.

changed_reading.before: The ayah compares a punished person with a saved person.
changed_reading.after: It compares two enacted trajectories: one is handled as an object and cast to a destination, while the other reaches the final assembly in a condition of settled security.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: I'malu ma shi'tum is enclosed by two occurrences of amal and the final bima ta'maluna basir.
baseline_models.mechanism: The apparent latitude of willing is bracketed by intentional work and comprehensive sight. Choice is real enough to produce deeds, but never supplies anonymity or escape from their visibility.

activation_trace.role: Purposeful action frames both the imperative and the final assessment, turning freedom into authored conduct.
Volition supplies the latitude under which the conduct is selected.
Discerning knowledge removes any inference that latitude entails unobserved action.

changed_reading.before: Do whatever you wish is an unrestricted permission or a generic threat.
changed_reading.after: It is an exposure test: willing remains operative, each choice becomes intentional work, and the enclosing sight makes that work inspectable.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus imperative returns the opponents' own challenge in 41:5. The intervening testimony scene makes work bodily disclosive, and 41:46 makes its consequence return to the actor; the command therefore hands their boast back as self-authored evidence.

activation_trace.role: Intentional work is the repeated focus hinge between the taunting command and divine inspection.
The same purposeful-action branch supplies the opponents' reciprocal challenge, which the focus command later echoes.
Attended witnessing converts past conduct into evidence presented against its doers.
Attempted covering identifies the failed strategy that the focus denial of hiddenness answers.
Purposeful action is explicitly assigned a consequence rather than left as transient behavior.
The actor's own self is the destination of that consequence, making the work reflexive.

structural_cues: 41:5 first voices 'work' as an oppositional challenge.
41:20-23 turn deeds into bodily testimony and expose the assumption that much action escaped knowledge.
41:46 assigns good or evil action for or against the actor's own self.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated work formula, failed covering, testimony, and reflexive consequence; I infer that 41:40 deliberately returns the earlier boast as an evidentiary command. A live alternative is that the repetition is thematic reinforcement without a direct rhetorical callback.

changed_reading.before: The imperative grants temporary latitude under surveillance.
changed_reading.after: The imperative is also a returned quotation-like challenge: keep producing the very work that bodies will disclose and that will come back for or against the worker.

context_deltas.mechanism: Across the surah, signs are articulated clearly while resistant hearers build a layered reception system of coverings, ear-weight, barrier, refusal, noise, blindness, and distance. Ilhad in the focus is thereby sharpened from a private wrong view into active rerouting and sabotage of how signs reach hearers.

activation_trace.role: A verbal turn or objection anchors ilhad in adversarial handling of communicated signs.
The sign remains an outward marker, so the failure lies in its handling rather than its absence.
Articulation into distinct parts and meanings supplies a deliberately clarified message channel.
A protective covering around the heart supplies an inward layer of blocked reception.
Auditory heaviness supplies a sensory layer that prevents uptake.
A preventing partition makes separation from the messenger an engineered relation.
Hearing as comprehension and compliance clarifies what the explicit refusal targets.
Mixed clamor supplies active acoustic interference meant to overpower the recitation.
Inner blindness names the terminal cognitive state produced by failed reception.
Distance turns an available call into one experienced as inaccessible.

structural_cues: 41:3 presents the signs as differentiated and intelligible.
41:4-5 answer that clarity with turning away, non-hearing, coverings, heaviness, and a barrier.
41:26 converts non-hearing into a deliberate noise tactic.
41:44 restages the result as ear-weight, blindness, and a call from far away.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies each reception barrier and their recurrence around explicit signs; I infer a cumulative causal architecture in which ilhad bends the channel of reception. A live alternative is that these are parallel descriptions of rejection rather than stages of one mechanism.

changed_reading.before: Ilhad means holding or voicing a deviant interpretation of signs.
changed_reading.after: Ilhad becomes the active manufacture of non-reception: a clear marker is diverted by shielding the interior, burdening the senses, adding noise, and converting nearness into experienced distance.

context_deltas.mechanism: 41:34-35 describes redirecting evil with what is better and twice says that this is only made available to particular recipients. The repeated passive l-q-y then makes the focus casting echo an allocation contrast: one may be made to receive the difficult better response, or be cast into fire, while secure arrival stands on the other side.

activation_trace.role: The focus uses forced casting to present the punitive allocation as something done to its recipient.
Beneficial good anchors the comparative question to the nearby command to answer with what is better.
Settled safety marks the opposed outcome of the allocation.
Goodness opposed to ugliness supplies both the quality of the response and the comparative 'better' that transforms the relation.
Pushing harm aside supplies an active redirection rather than passive retaliation.
What a person is made to encounter of good or difficulty supplies the lexical bridge between ethical reception and final fate.
Self-restraint identifies the disposition able to receive and sustain the counter-response.
An allotted share makes reception sound like a granted portion rather than mere comprehension.

structural_cues: 41:34 commands a redirection of evil capable of converting an enemy into an intimate ally.
41:35 repeats the passive l-q-y form around patience and a great allotted share.
41:40 reuses passive l-q-y for casting while contrasting it with secure arrival.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the local passive-root repetition, the better response, and the allotted share; I infer an allocative parallel between receiving a transformative ethic and receiving a punitive fate. The materially live alternative is a stylistic root recurrence with no causal bridge between 41:35 and 41:40.

changed_reading.before: The fire/security contrast is only a future sorting of already fixed classes.
changed_reading.after: The contrast also echoes present receptivity: the capacity to receive and enact the difficult better response stands against being passively allocated to fire.

context_deltas.mechanism: The promise in 41:30-32 gives security a social and spatial texture: straight continuation, descending messengers, removal of anticipated harm, allied accompaniment, and prepared hospitality. The one who comes secure in the focus thus completes an already accompanied trajectory rather than merely escaping punishment.

activation_trace.role: Arrival supplies the endpoint of a trajectory that the preceding promise begins before resurrection.
Inner settledness under freedom from harm names the focus outcome clarified by the earlier reassurance.
The final rising fixes the public endpoint at which accompanied security is displayed.
Straightness and maintained balance supply the lived trajectory leading toward secure arrival.
The descent of messengers supplies accompaniment that meets the steadfast before the final endpoint.
Expected future harm is explicitly removed, specifying the prospective content of security.
Loving alliance and support make security relational rather than merely juridical.
Prepared reception for an arriving guest gives the secure destination a hospitality structure.

structural_cues: 41:30 joins steadfastness to a descent that removes fear and grief.
41:31 extends allied support across present and future life.
41:32 names the promised destination as prepared reception for a guest.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies reassurance, continuity of alliance, and hospitality; I infer that these specify the texture and pathway of aminan in 41:40. A live alternative is that 41:30-32 is a parallel promise without defining the later term.

changed_reading.before: Coming secure means arriving exempt from the fire.
changed_reading.after: Coming secure is the completion of a straight, accompanied passage into prepared hospitality, with fear already displaced by an enduring alliance.

context_deltas.mechanism: The material sign in revived earth, the outward signs in the horizons, the inward signs in selves, and the final encompassing closure leave no exterior side to which ilhad can escape. The focus denial of hiddenness becomes spatial as well as epistemic.

activation_trace.role: Inclining toward a supposed refuge supplies the attempted escape route.
Movement to an edge supplies the geometry tested by the surah's inside-out sign field.
Visible markers anchor the field in phenomena that disclose rather than conceal.
The same marker branch identifies the immediately preceding earth scene as part of the sign field.
The earth's life-bearing movement makes the sign materially enacted, not only verbally stated.
Far outward regions extend the sign field to the limits of viewed space.
The person's own self supplies the corresponding inward location of disclosure.
Emergence into clarity names what the outside-and-inside display is moving toward.
Complete cognitive enclosure closes the geometry by denying an unobserved outside.

structural_cues: 41:39 places an enacted sign in the revived earth immediately before the focus.
41:53 distributes signs across the horizons and the observers' own selves until truth becomes clear.
41:54 ends with comprehensive enclosure after naming doubt about meeting.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies outward, inward, material, and encompassing locations; I infer a closed sign topology in which lateral refuge is impossible. A live alternative is that the spatial terms accumulate rhetorically without forming a deliberate enclosure model.

changed_reading.before: Those who deviate within particular signs cannot hide their conduct from God.
changed_reading.after: They try to move toward an edge inside a sign field that spans earth, horizons, and self and is itself encompassed; hiddenness fails because there is no exterior position.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediate continuation shifts from the visibility of those attacking signs to the resilience of the reminder and book: falsehood cannot reach it from either direction. Ilhad therefore changes the condition of the actor and audience, not the integrity of the sign-bearing text; the failed attack exposes its agent.

activation_trace.role: Adversarial verbal turning anchors the attempted attack on communicated signs.
Removal of hiddenness makes the actor, rather than a damaged text, what is brought into disclosure.
Blocking or veiling truth locates the failure in reception of the reminder.
Ordered written discourse identifies the sign-bearing object that remains intact.
Resistance to being reached supplies the book's protected inaccessibility to corruption.
The denied act of arrival frames falsehood as unable to reach the text from any route.
Loss of truth or stability names the corrupting content whose entry is excluded.
Tight construction and reliability explain why the communicated object withstands the attempted approach.

structural_cues: 41:40 says the agents of ilhad are not hidden.
41:41 immediately names rejection of the reminder while describing the book as inaccessible to defeat.
41:42 denies falsehood any approach from before or behind and grounds the book in wise construction.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies actor-visibility followed by textual resilience; I infer a reversal in which distortion reveals the distorter without penetrating the book. A live alternative is that the two claims are adjacent assurances rather than one failed-attack mechanism.

changed_reading.before: The warning says distortion is detected and punished.
changed_reading.after: It also separates effect from intention: distortion can obstruct a hearer, but it cannot enter and destabilize the text; instead, the attempt renders its agent visible.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the light branch of the fire root and could wrongly collapse fire into illumination. It remains anchored because fire stands between denied hiddenness and divine sight, while the surah places fire beside witnessing and earlier luminous lamps. Downstream prose should present it only as a root-family and compositional echo of exposure, not as the lexical meaning of al-nar.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Al-nar occurs inside a sentence framed by la yakhfawna and basir.

activation_trace.role: Actual burning fire preserves the literal punitive destination of the focus contrast.
The root-family's luminous branch adds an exploratory exposure echo without replacing the fire sense.
Visual apprehension makes exposure a live compositional function around the fire.
Lamps establish controlled luminosity as a displayed feature of the ordered heavens.
The earlier fire destination begins the public gathering sequence that leads into testimony.
Present witnessing turns that destination sequence into an evidentiary scene.

changed_reading.before: Fire functions only as the punitive destination in the comparison.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, being cast into fire also completes the collapse of concealment: punishment occurs in a compositional field of exposure, sight, and testimony.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because the grave-side and refuge branches are materially distant from ordinary ilhad in signs. It remains anchored to the focus root and gains a coherent spatial contrast from casting, permanent fire-lodging, and prepared hospitality elsewhere in the surah. Downstream prose should label it a material analogy, never a replacement gloss or a claim that the ayah literally describes burial architecture.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The side-cut and refuge branches of l-h-d meet the focus contrast between being cast away and arriving secure.

activation_trace.role: A chamber cut into a side supplies the exploratory image of making concealment inside an already bounded structure.
Inclining toward shelter gives that side movement the attempted function of refuge.
A cast-off object supplies the opposed loss of protected placement.
A fixed lodging gives the fire a grim dwelling structure rather than a momentary contact.
Prepared guest-reception supplies the counter-space for the secure arriver.

changed_reading.before: Ilhad is an abstract deviation followed by one of two outcomes.
changed_reading.after: As a contained material analogy, the deviator cuts toward a false side-refuge but ends as a cast-off in punitive lodging, while secure arrival is met by genuine hospitality.

strongest_changes: The work imperative returns the opponents' own 41:5 challenge after the surah has made deeds bodily self-disclosing and reflexive.
Ilhad becomes a cumulative practice of engineered non-reception rather than only an incorrect proposition about signs.
The passive l-q-y recurrence in 41:35 and 41:40 opens an allocative contrast between receiving the difficult better response and being cast into fire.
Signs distributed through revived earth, horizons, and selves, then closed by encompassing knowledge, turn failed hiddenness into a no-exterior spatial model.
The immediate 41:41-42 continuation distinguishes obstruction of hearers from any successful penetration of the resilient book.
summary.what_was_special: The whole-surah packet exposed long-range recurrences of work, covering, hearing, testimony, passive l-q-y, hospitality, and inside-outside geometry that a focus-only reading leaves disconnected.
remaining_uncertainties: The ethical-allocation link through l-q-y may be deliberate local architecture or only conspicuous verbal recurrence.
The 41:30-32 promise strongly textures aminan, but it may remain a parallel promise rather than a direct specification.
The closed sign field and fire-as-exposure models depend on compositional inference beyond ordinary lexical force.
The grave-side/refuge model is useful only as a carefully contained material analogy.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Sideward interpretation cannot produce concealment.** **ل ح د B001/B005** gives deviation from straightness and sideward skew; **ء ي ي B003** gives visible signs; **خ ف ي B001/B003** gives hiddenness and its removal. The first clause directly opposes interpretive inclination to failed concealment. I infer that bending the sign changes the reader's course, not the sign's visibility to its source.
2. **Two orientations terminate in two modes of arrival.** **ل ق ي B005** gives casting something where it is met; **ء ت ي B001** gives coming; **ء م ن B001** secure trust; **ق و م B013** resurrection and rising. One is cast into fire, the other comes secure. I infer that present action fixes whether agency is retained at the endpoint. The command to work, closed by **ب ص ر B001/B002**, makes that directional contrast practical.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 41:46 later states the reflexive consequence of action, clarifying why the endpoint tracks present work. 41:52–54 develops sideward deviation into distant schism and finally places all supposed concealment within complete enclosure.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Deviation reroutes signs but cannot reroute observation.** Lexically, `ل ح د B001` is deviation from right and `ل ح د B005` sideward skew, `خ ف ي B001` hiddenness, and `ب ص ر B002` penetrating inner sight. Structurally, deviation occurs “in” the signs, concealment is negated, and the final statement returns sight to their work; this follows 41:39’s visibly ordered sign. I assign ilhad the role of bending evidentiary direction and divine sight the role of preserving the acts and relations the bend attempts to hide. The inferred arrow is that interpretive rerouting affects the agent’s path, not the sign’s visibility to the observer. The ayah reads distortion as self-positioning under observation.

2. **Being cast contrasts with arriving securely.** `ل ق ي B005` is casting or throwing down, `ء ت ي B001` coming/arriving, and `ء م ن B001` settled security. The comparison sets passive `يُلقى` against active `يأتي` before the command to act. I assign casting the role of dispossessed movement and secure arrival the role of agentive approach. The abductive move is that present action shapes whether one finally retains orientation or is handled as an object. The contrast reads as two modes of arrival, not only two destinations.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 41:42’s before/behind protection mirrored the no-hiddenness claim: both actor and book are exposed across all approach directions, but only the book is inaccessible to corrupting entry. 41:44 then located failure in the receiver’s ear and insight.

baseline.text: Ayetlerimiz konusunda eğriliğe sapanlar bizden gizli kalmaz. Ateşe atılan mı daha iyidir, yoksa kıyamet günü güven içinde gelen mi? Dilediğinizi yapın; şüphesiz O yaptıklarınızı görmektedir.

findings.text: İşaretleri yana eğerek yorumlamak gözlemden kaçış sağlamaz; yalnızca yorumlayanın kendi yönünü saptırır.

Ateşe edilgen biçimde atılmakla güven içinde etkin biçimde gelmek arasındaki fark, bugünkü eylemin son varışta yönünü koruyan bir özne mi yoksa taşınan bir nesne mi olunacağını belirlediğini gösterir.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, ortak çekirdeği doğru yoldan, haktan ve doğru amaçtan ayrılma olarak kurar; inançtan uzaklaşma, haksızlığa yönelme ve Tanrı'nın adlarını uygunsuz biçimde yorumlama bu çekirdeğin özel gerçekleşmeleridir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal yalnızca değer, inanç ve hak ölçüsünden sapmayı kapsar; mezarın yan oyuğu, sığınma ve salt fiziksel yana kayma öteki dallara aittir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Dal hem tek başına kullanılan biçimleri hem de belirli söz öbeklerine bağlı özel anlamları içerir; kutsal alan, Tanrı'nın adları ve inanç türleriyle ilgili ayrıntılar bütün yalın kullanımlara yayılmaz.

concept_map.definition: Doğru yoldan, haktan ya da doğru amaçtan ayrılıp yanlış olana yönelmedir. İnançtan uzaklaşma, kutsal bir yerde haksızlığa yönelme ve Tanrı'nın adlarını uygunsuz niteliklerle açıklama bunun bağlama bağlı özel biçimleridir.

facets.statement: Doğru yoldan, haktan veya doğru amaçtan ayrılarak yanlış olana yönelme.
İnanç alanında doğru kabul edilen yoldan uzaklaşma ve inancı zedeleyen ya da geçersiz kılan bir ortak koşmaya yönelme.
Kutsal sayılan bir yerde doğru davranıştan ayrılıp haksızlığa yönelme.
Tanrı'nın adlarına uygun olmayan nitelikler yükleme veya onları yakışıksız biçimde yorumlama.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, anlamı doğru ve haklı çizgiden ayrılma çevresinde birleştirir. Toplu kanıt, bu sapmanın genel bir yanlış yönelişten inanç, kutsal yerde haksızlık ve Tanrı'nın adlarının uygunsuz açıklanması gibi özel bağlamlara uzandığını gösterir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Dalın değer ve inanç ölçüsüne bağlı ortak çekirdeğini karşılar; özel bağlamların ayrıntıları gerektiğinde ayrıca belirtilir.

error_profile.preserves: Doğru kabul edilen çizgiden ayrılma ve yanlış olana yönelme çekirdeğini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Doğru yol, doğru amaç veya hak ölçüsünden ayrılmayı anlatan genel kullanımlarda uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Hak ve doğruluk ölçüsünden ayrılma anlamını doğal bir eylem olarak korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Sapmanın özellikle inanç alanındaki doğru kabul edilen yoldan uzaklaşma olduğu bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: İnanç alanındaki yön değişimini ve doğru kabul edilen yoldan ayrılmayı korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Kutsal sayılan yerde doğru davranıştan ayrılma ve haksızlığa yönelme anlatıldığında uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Yerle sınırlı haksız yönelişi ve doğru davranıştan ayrılma koşulunu korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Tanrı'nın adlarına uygun olmayan nitelikler yükleme veya onları yakışıksız açıklama bağlamında kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Adları uygunsuz niteliklerle açıklama ve doğru anlam çizgisinden uzaklaştırma özelliğini korur.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Hak, inanç ve doğru amaç bakımından değer yüklü sapmayı ve bunun özel kullanımlarını kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Fiziksel yol doğrultusundan ayrılmayı ve bir topluluğun sağa sola kaymasını da kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal da doğru veya düz kabul edilen bir çizgiden ayrılma düşüncesini taşır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Komşu dal genel ve fiziksel doğrultu sapmasına kadar uzanırken bu dal hak, inanç ve doğru amaç ölçüsünden yanlış olana yönelişle sınırlıdır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: İnançtan ayrılma, kutsal yerde haksızlık ve Tanrı'nın adlarını uygunsuz açıklama kapsamlarını taşır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Yargıda, niyette ve işte adaletten ayrılmayı ve günaha bilerek yönelmeyi özellikle kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal da doğru amaçtan ve haktan ayrılıp haksızlığa yönelme alanında örtüşür.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Komşu dal yargı ve niyet başta olmak üzere adaletsiz yönelişi öne çıkarır; bu dalın ayırıcı alanı inanç ve adlandırmayla ilgili özel sapmalardır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: İnanç yolundan uzaklaşma ile kutsal yer ve Tanrı'nın adlarıyla ilgili özel kullanımları kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Bir karşı tarafa haksızlık etmeyi ve doğrudan uzak bir söz söylemeyi belirginleştirir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her ikisi de haktan ayrılma ve haksız bir yana yönelme çekirdeğinde buluşur.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Komşu dal karşı tarafa karşı haksızlık ve gerçeğe uzak söz çevresinde daralır; bu dal daha geniş bir değer ve inanç sapmasını anlatır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Doğru, haklı ve inanca uygun kabul edilen çizgiden değer yüklü ayrılmayı anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Bir nesnenin kenarını veya fiziksel olarak bir yana sapmasını anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dalda da bir merkezden veya doğrultudan yana ayrılma imgesi bulunur.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal ölçüsel ve değer yüklü bir yanlış yöneliştir; komşu dal ise kenar, yan ve somut doğrultu değişikliğiyle ilgilidir.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Gösterilen bütün komşular değerlendirildi; seçilen dört karşılaştırma hak, adalet ve fiziksel sapma sınırlarını en iyi belirledi. Yasak, bağışlama, günah ve öteki iç dallar yalnızca aynı konu alanını paylaşan ya da burada yinelenen daha uzak karşılaştırmalar olduğu için yayımlanmadı.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, mezarın ortasında olmayan ve yan duvarında ya da enine açılan eğimli oyuğu açıkça tanımlar. Kazma ve ölüyü bu oyuğa yerleştirme anlamları aynı nesneye bağlı eylemlerdir, fakat oyuk kavramının kendisiyle bir tutulmaz.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal mezarın tümünü veya ortadaki çukuru değil, özellikle yan tarafta açılan oyuğu anlatır; kazma ve yerleştirme yalnızca ilgili eylem biçimlerinde geçerlidir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Dal, yan oyuk adını ve bu oyuğun kazılması ya da ölünün içine yerleştirilmesiyle sınırlı eylem biçimlerini birlikte barındırır; eylem anlamları yalın nesne tanımına eklenmez.

concept_map.definition: Mezarın ortasında değil, yan duvarında veya enine açılan ve içine ölü yerleştirilen eğimli oyuktur. Oyuğu kazma ve ölüyü oraya yerleştirme, bu çekirdeğe bağlı özel eylem kullanımlarıdır.

facets.statement: Mezarın yan tarafında ya da enine açılmış, merkezden yana kayan özel oyuk.
Aynı oyuk, mezarın yanındaki yarık veya ortadan yana eğilen çukur olarak da betimlenir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak tanımı, mezarın orta çukurundan ayrılan ve yan tarafta ya da enine açılan özel bir oyuktur. Değişen betimlemeler, ayrı nesneler değil aynı yapının yan konumunu ve merkezden eğimini anlatır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Mezarın tamamını değil, yan duvarında ölünün yerleştirilmesi için açılan özel oyuğu adlandırır.

error_profile.preserves: Mezar bağlamını, yan konumu ve özel oyuk olma özelliğini birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Yapının mezarın yan duvarında açıldığını açıkça belirtmek gereken anlatımlarda uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Yapının mezara bağlı, yan tarafta açılan bir oyuk olduğunu eksiksiz korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Oyuğun mezarın merkezinden yana kaymış ve eğimli oluşunu açıklayan bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Mezar içindeki yan konumu, çukur biçimini ve merkezden eğilme özelliğini korur.

error_profile.preserves: Ölü gömme yapısıyla ilgili genel ortamı korur.
error_profile.adds: Yan oyuk dışındaki bütün mezar yapısını ve bölümlerini de kavrama katar.
error_profile.collision: Mezarın tamamıyla onun yan tarafındaki özel oyuğu birbirine karıştırır.

error_profile.preserves: Mezar içinde açılmış bir çukur olma niteliğini korur.
error_profile.adds: Ortada açılan sıradan mezar çukurunu da kapsar ve yan konum sınırını kaldırır.
error_profile.collision: Yan duvardaki özel oyukla mezarın ana çukurunu karıştırabilir.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Mezarın yan duvarında açılan özel oyuğu ve ona bağlı işlemleri belirtir.

neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal ölü gömme yapısı ve ölünün mezara yerleştirilmesi alanında buluşur.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Komşu dal bütün mezarı ve gömme eylemini anlatır; bu dal mezarın yalnızca yan tarafındaki özel mimari bölümdür.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Ölü gömmeye ayrılmış bir mezarın yanındaki belirli oyuğu anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Yerde, bulutta veya dağda bulunan genel açıklık, boşluk ve geniş aralığı kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dalda da bir yüzey ya da kütle içinde açılmış boşluk düşüncesi vardır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Komşu dal herhangi bir doğal açıklık veya boşluktur; bu dalın konumu, işlevi ve mezar yapısına bağlılığı zorunludur.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Ölünün yerleştirildiği yan oyuğun yapısını ve konumunu belirtir.

neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal aynı ölü gömme sürecinin farklı öğelerinde yer alabilir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal bir mezar bölümünün adıdır; komşu dal ise toprağı dökme ve örtme eylemidir, bu nedenle anlam çekirdekleri örtüşmez.

neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Herhangi bir nesnenin kenarını ve fiziksel olarak bir yana sapmayı kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Mezar oyuğunun yanda bulunması ile genel kenar ve yana yönelme düşüncesi ortak bir uzamsal alan oluşturur.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün komşular gözden geçirildi; mezarın bütünü, genel oyuk, toprakla gömme ve fiziksel yan kavramlarıyla yapılan dört karşılaştırma sınırı en açık biçimde gösterdi. Örtme, mezar sağlama, yükselti ve öteki iç dallar daha uzak ya da yinelenen bağlar sunduğu için eklenmedi.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi hem sığınılan yeri hem de bir şeye ya da yere yönelip sığınma eylemini açıkça destekler. Yana yönelme burada bağımsız bir fiziksel hareket değil, sığınağa ulaşmanın ilişkisel parçasıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, korunmak için yönelinen sığınak ve ona sığınma ile sınırlıdır; haktan sapma, mezar oyuğu veya genel kenar anlamını kapsamaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yer bildiren biçim sığınağı, bir şeye yönelmeyi belirten yapı ise sığınma eylemini anlatır; yer ve eylem yüzleri korunur ve yalın bir yana eğilme anlamında birleştirilmez.

concept_map.definition: Korunmak için yönelinen sığınak veya böyle bir yere yönelip sığınma eylemidir. Yönelme, burada sığınma ilişkisini kurar ve salt yana hareket anlamına gelmez.

facets.statement: Kendisinde korunma aranarak sığınılan yer.
Bir şeye veya yere yönelerek ona sığınma eylemi.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, sığınılan yer ile o yere yönelip sığınma eylemini aynı ilişkisel yapı içinde verir. Ortak anlam, korunma sağlayan hedefi ve kişinin o hedefe yönelişini birbirinden ayırarak birlikte açıklar.

concept_gloss.applicability: Yer bildiren ve o yere yönelme bildiren kullanımların ortak haritasını, iki yüzü birbirine karıştırmadan karşılar.

error_profile.preserves: Sığınağın kendisini, ona yönelmeyi ve sığınma ilişkisini birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Korunmak için başvurulan yerin veya hedefin adlandırıldığı bağlamlarda doğal karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Korunma amacıyla sığınılan yer olma özelliğini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir kimsenin bir şeye ya da yere yönelerek onda korunma aradığı eylem bağlamlarında kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Hedefe yönelme ile sığınma eylemini aynı ilişkide tutar.
Bir sıkıntıdan uzaklaşma ve korunma arama yönünü kısmen korur.
error_profile.loses: Sığınılan yerin kendisini ve belirli bir hedefe yönelip onda korunma bulma ilişkisini siler.
error_profile.collision: Hedefi olan sığınmayı yalnızca tehlikeden uzaklaşma hareketiyle karıştırır.

error_profile.preserves: Korunmaya elverişli bir yer olma özelliğini korur.
error_profile.loses: O yere yönelip sığınma eylemi yüzünü karşılamaz.
error_profile.collision: Uzun süreli kalma yeri anlamıyla geçici sığınma hedefini karıştırabilir.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Sığınağa doğru yana yönelme ilişkisini yer ve eylem yüzleriyle birlikte belirginleştirir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Güvenli yere varma, kurtulma ve korunaklı yere gitme sonucunu özellikle öne çıkarır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal da güvenlik arayan kişinin bir sığınağa yönelmesini anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Komşu dal güvenliğe erişme ve kurtulma sonucunu daha güçlü taşır; bu dalın ayırıcı yanı sığınılan hedefe yönelme ilişkisidir.

neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Sığınağın yanında kaçış, aranılan hedef ve yardım bulma anlamlarına da uzanır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal da başvurulan sığınak ve ona yönelme alanında büyük ölçüde örtüşür.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Komşu dal kaçış ve yardım arayışı gibi daha geniş sonuçları kapsar; bu dal sığınak ile ona yönelip sığınma bağına odaklanır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Yer veya şey olarak sığınağı ve ona doğru yönelmeyi anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Bir kişiden, varlıktan ya da şeyden korunma istemeyi ve ona tutunarak güvence aramayı da kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dalda da tehlikeye karşı bir koruyucu hedefe başvurma ve sığınma vardır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Komşu dal koruma isteğini ve koruyucuya tutunmayı öne çıkarır; bu dal sığınılan yer ile ona yönelme ilişkisini adlandırır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Sığınağın kendisini ve ona yönelerek sığınma eylemini belirtir.

neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal korunma arayan kişinin bir dayanağa başvurması durumunda kesişir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dalın çekirdeği sığınma hedefi ve ona yöneliştir; komşu dalın çekirdeği ise engelleyen, koruyan tutma veya tutunmadır.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar değerlendirildi; seçilenler sığınak, kurtuluş, korunma ve tutunma arasındaki en yakın dört sınırı gösterir. Yardım çağırma, kötülüğü uzaklaştırma ve öteki iç dallar ya daha uzak bir olay ilişkisi kurduğu ya da seçilen ayrımları yinelediği için eklenmedi.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi konuşma alanını destekler, ancak tek bir birleşik eylem vermez: sözün bir hedefe yönelmesi, bir söyleyiş biçiminde itiraz etme ve ayrı bir biçimde tartışıp çekişme anlamları yan yana durur. Dal korunabilir, fakat bu yüzler tek bir genel konuşma anlamı gibi kaynaştırılmamalıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal yalnızca belirtilen söz ve söyleyiş yapılarına bağlıdır; genel hitap, her türlü tartışma veya değer bakımından haktan sapma anlamına genişletilemez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Sözü bir hedefe yöneltme belirli bir söz yapısına, yönelme ile itiraz arasındaki ayrım belirli söyleyişlere, tartışma anlamı ise ayrı bir eylem biçimine bağlıdır; bu yüzler yalın ve sınırsız bir konuşma anlamında birleştirilmez.

concept_map.definition: Sözü belirli bir hedefe yöneltmek veya belirli bir söyleyişte ona yönelmek ya da itiraz etmektir. Ayrı bir eylem biçimi, karşılıklı görüş ileri sürüp tartışmayı anlatır.

facets.statement: Sözü veya dili belirli bir hedefe yöneltme.
Belirli bir söyleyişin hedefe yönelme ya da ona itiraz etme biçiminde anlaşılması.
Karşılıklı görüş ileri sürerek tartışma ve çekişme.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Toplu kanıt, konuşma alanında üç ilişkili fakat ayrı yüz gösterir: sözün bir hedefe yöneltilmesi, bir söyleyişin yönelme ya da itiraz olarak anlaşılması ve tartışmaya girme. Bu ayrım, kaynaklar arasındaki karşılık farkını herhangi bir kaynağa tek başına yüklemeden korur.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi fiziksel yana sapmayı desteklemekle birlikte yalnızca hareket bildirmez; bir şeyin kenarı veya yanı da açıkça adlandırılır. Eğri kuyu ve hedefin bir yanına kayan ok, bu iki uzamsal yüzün özel örnekleridir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Bir şeyin kenarını bildiren adlandırma, genel fiziksel sapma biçimi ve kuyu ile oka bağlı özel yapılar ayrı tutulur; kuyu veya ok örneği bütün yalın kullanımlara yayılmaz.
